cli.help.text:
ergo <command> — install and run ergo

  start                 Start ergo (through the service manager; starts the service manager first if needed)
  stop                  Stop ergo
  restart               Restart ergo
  status [--json]       Is ergo / the service manager running, which version, where it is installed
  logs [-n lines] [-f]  Show ergo's log (-f keeps following; Ctrl+C to quit)
  open [--print]        Open ergo's web page in the browser
  update [--check] [--version <version>] [--from <url>] [--mirror cn|github]
                        Update: the new version goes into a new folder and is switched in when ergo is idle; the old one is kept
  rollback              Switch back to the previous version
  uninstall [--yes] [--delete-data | --keep-data]
                        Uninstall: remove it from PATH, the service manager and autostart; asks whether to delete your data
  components list | add <id> | remove <id> | import <file or folder>
                        Components: embedding model, voice, Claude Code (downloaded on demand)
  svc <command…>        Passed through to the service manager (ergo svc status is lsm status; lsm is its short name)
  onboard               First-run setup (in progress; for now it just starts ergo)
  version               Version

ergo's data lives in ~/.ergo (set ERGO_DATA_DIR to change it) and the service manager's in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ergo\supervisor (LSM_DATA_DIR); updating or uninstalling the program never touches them.
cli.status.managerDown: Service manager: not running (ergo start starts it)
cli.svc.managerNoAnswer: The service manager was started but port {port} never answered. See its log: {log}
cli.svc.startingManager: The service manager is not running; starting it (port {port})…
cli.stop.managerDown: The service manager is not running, so ergo is not running under it either.
cli.logs.none: No log yet ({file}): ergo has not been started through the service manager.
cli.onboard.notYet: The first-run setup is still being built (ergo onboard, doctor and key set come next). Starting ergo for now; set your model key in the web page under Settings · Models.
cli.update.npm: This ergo was installed with npm: update with npm i -g ergo-ai@latest, remove with npm rm -g ergo-ai.
cli.update.scoop: This ergo was installed with Scoop: update it with scoop update ergo.
cli.update.winget: This ergo was installed with winget: update it with winget upgrade.
cli.update.dev: This ergo runs from the repository: git pull, npm ci and npm run build are the update.
cli.update.link: This is a dev link to a working folder: git pull and npm run build there and it takes effect.
cli.update.sourceCheck: Built from source ({ref}): ergo update pulls the new code of that branch or tag, rebuilds it and switches over when ergo is idle.
cli.update.sourceFailed: Building the new version from source failed; the version in use was not touched.
cli.update.noInstallScript: Cannot find the install script {file}; updating a source install needs it.
cli.update.available: Version {version} is available (you have {current}): run ergo update.
cli.update.noPublicKey: This ergo has no release public key yet, so the new version's signature cannot be checked; not installing. Add --allow-unsigned to install anyway (at your own risk).
cli.update.downloadFailed: Download failed: {detail} (run ergo update again to resume)
cli.update.verifyFailed: The new version failed verification; not installing: {detail}
cli.update.unsigned: Signature not checked (--allow-unsigned); only the checksum was verified.
cli.update.badPackage: The package does not contain version {version}; not installing.
cli.download.checksum: the download does not match the checksums ({detail})
cli.download.unreachable: no address could be downloaded from ({detail})
cli.switch.waitingIdle: Waiting for ergo to be idle (it is not stopped while a task runs or an action with side effects is in progress)…
cli.switch.idleTimeout: ergo stayed busy for a long time, so the switch was skipped. Run it again when ergo is idle (or wait longer with --idle-timeout <seconds>).
cli.switch.restarted: ergo is up on the new version.
cli.switch.failed: Could not switch: {detail} (the version in use is unchanged)
cli.switch.restartedOld: ergo is up again on the previous version.
cli.switch.pruneBusy: Old versions {versions} are still in use; they will be removed on the next update.
cli.rollback.none: There is no previous version to switch back to.
cli.uninstall.npm: This ergo was installed with npm: remove it with npm rm -g ergo-ai. Your data is in ~/.ergo; delete it yourself if you no longer need it.
cli.uninstall.scoop: This ergo was installed with Scoop: remove it with scoop uninstall ergo (your data in ~/.ergo stays; delete it yourself if you no longer need it).
cli.uninstall.winget: This ergo was installed with winget: remove it with winget uninstall (your data in ~/.ergo stays; delete it yourself if you no longer need it).
cli.uninstall.dev: This ergo runs from the repository; it is not installed, so there is nothing to uninstall.
cli.uninstall.notInstallDir: {dir} does not look like an ergo install folder; not deleting it.
cli.uninstall.plan: About to uninstall ergo: stop it, remove it from the service manager and autostart, remove {bin} from PATH and delete the install folder {dir}.
cli.uninstall.otherServices: The service manager also runs other services ({services}). Its program is in the folder being deleted, so it stops too (those services keep running, just unsupervised).
cli.uninstall.askData: Delete your data too? ergo's data {data} and the service manager's data {svc} (kept by default) (y/N)
cli.uninstall.managerStillUp: The service manager (pid {pid}) did not stop; it was not started by ergo. End it in Task Manager.
cli.uninstall.autostartElsewhere: The autostarted service manager belongs to another install; left it alone.
cli.uninstall.pathRemoved: Removed {bin} from your user PATH (new terminals pick it up).
cli.uninstall.dataKept: Data kept: {data}, {svc} (a reinstall picks it up; delete it yourself if you no longer need it).
cli.uninstall.done: Uninstalled; the install folder {dir} is deleted after this command exits.
cli.components.col.title: Name
cli.components.unknown: No such component: {id} (see ergo components list)
cli.components.needId: Give a component id, e.g. ergo components add bge-m3
cli.components.needFile: Give a file or folder, e.g. ergo components import D:\Downloads\bge-m3
cli.components.usage: Usage: ergo components list | add <id> | remove <id> | import <file or folder>
cli.components.daemonDown: ergo is not running ({url} does not answer): run ergo start first.
